intro: There are a variety of reasons that individuals use and abuse benzodiazepines other than taking them as prescribed to them. Studies show that the most common reason individuals take benzos is to relieve tension and to help them feel relaxed. Other reasons identified were getting help sleeping, managing emotions, experimenting, and increasing the effects of other substances.

sections.title: What Are Benzodiazepines?
body: Benzodiazepines are a class of prescribed medications that are often used to treat individuals who are living with severe anxiety disorders, such as pain disorders. Examples of medications included in this class are Valium, Klonopin, Ativan, and Xanax. These medications can also be used as muscle relaxants and to ease symptoms associated with alcohol withdrawal.

sections.title: How Are Benzos Used?
body: When taken as prescribed, benzos can be used to effectively manage symptoms associated with anxiety disorders, insomnia, seizures, and alcohol withdrawal.

More often than not, individuals who misuse and abuse benzos are poly-drug users, which means that they use more than one substance. A dangerous combination would be the use of benzos and opioids, as they can both slow down our breathing. The National Institute on Drug Abuse reported that 16% of opioid overdose deaths in 2016 also involved benzodiazepines.

sections.title: Are Benzos Addictive?
body: Benzodiazepines are addictive substances because of the way that they impact our brains. When someone takes a benzo, their brain releases a large amount of Dopamine. Dopamine is a naturally occurring chemical in our brain that plays a role in our reward cycle. When Dopamine is released, we feel good, which reinforces the behavior we just engaged in. When someone takes a benzo, there is a surge of Dopamine released, which is more than what would be released with other enjoyable activities.
